items.title: Docetaxel and SX-682 for Advanced Prostate Cancer Trial
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is testing a new drug called SX-682 combined with docetaxel chemotherapy in patients whose advanced prostate cancer has returned or spread. The study includes patients with head/neck cancers and prostate cancer. SX-682 is taken as a pill and combined with standard docetaxel treatment.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combinations in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large phase 1/2 study tests the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab combined with various treatments (including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, and others) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial has 10 different treatment groups testing different combination approaches. It is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: HLD-0915 Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial is testing the safety and effectiveness of HLD-0915, a new investigational drug, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have already tried other treatments. The study is currently recruiting patients and will evaluate this treatment in different prostate cancer populations.

items.title: Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, and Cabozantinib for Rare Genitourinary Tumors
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether combining two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) with the targeted drug cabozantinib works for patients with rare genitourinary tumors including some prostate cancers. The study is recruiting patients whose tumors have spread and who have no other treatment options.

items.title: BNT324 Versus Docetaxel Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares a new drug called BNT324 to standard docetaxel chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have been treated with hormone therapy but not chemotherapy. The study will measure how long patients live without cancer progression and overall survival. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: STEAP1 CAR-T Cell Therapy With Enzalutamide for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests a novel CAR-T cell therapy targeting STEAP1 protein combined with enzalutamide hormone therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. CAR-T therapy genetically modifies a patient's own immune cells to attack cancer cells. The study is recruiting and evaluating safety and effectiveness of this immunotherapy approach.

items.title: FTT PET/CT Scan Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This imaging study uses a new PET scan tracer called FTT to measure PARP enzyme activity in cancer sites. Up to 30 men with metastatic prostate cancer will have scans before and possibly after starting new treatment. The goal is to see if this scan can help predict treatment response.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests the safety of xaluritamig (an investigational immunotherapy) combined with standard hormone drugs (darolutamide or abiraterone) in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients to determine safe dosing of this combination approach.

items.title: BMS-986365 Versus Standard Treatment Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares the effectiveness and safety of BMS-986365 (a new investigational drug) versus the doctor's choice of standard therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting and will measure survival and other outcomes.

items.title: Xaluritamig Safety Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety of xaluritamig, an investigational immunotherapy drug, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients and will determine the appropriate dosing regimen for this treatment.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares luxdegalutamide (a hormone therapy) combined with lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy versus PSMA therapy alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with hormone therapy and possibly chemotherapy. The study is no longer recruiting and testing two different doses.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig plus abiraterone hormone therapy versus standard treatments (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to measure overall survival. The study is recruiting.

items.title: Nezastomig With or Without Cemiplimab in mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests the safety and effectiveness of nezastomig (an investigational immunotherapy) alone or combined with cemiplimab in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and other tumors. The study has dose-finding and expansion phases and is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies lutetium Lu 177 dotatate, a radioactive drug therapy, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has neuroendocrine features. This treatment targets and delivers radiation specifically to neuroendocrine tumor cells. The trial is recruiting patients whose cancer has spread despite other treatments.

items.title: Tinengotinib Plus Standard Treatments in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests whether tinengotinib combined with abiraterone or enzalutamide is safe and tolerable in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if adding tinengotinib to standard hormone therapy causes few or manageable side effects. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: DNA Vaccines Plus Pembrolizumab in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests DNA vaccines (pTVG-HP and pTVG-AR) combined with pembrolizumab immunotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study compares using one versus two vaccines to see which approach creates stronger immune responses and better tumor control. Treatment continues for up to 2 years.

items.title: Radium-223 With M3814 and Avelumab in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial compares radium-223 radiation treatment alone, with M3814, or with M3814 plus avelumab immunotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find the best dose and determine which combination works best. Currently suspended.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Development
items.summary: This research paper explains how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL6/STAT3 signaling pathways, drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. These inflammatory signals work together with androgen receptor signaling to promote cancer growth, spread, and resistance to therapy. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to new treatment strategies.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA that triggers strong immune responses against prostate cancer. The vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases in animal models. When combined with PD-1 immunotherapy, it significantly improved tumor control and extended survival, suggesting promise for future clinical trials.

items.title: Metformin Reduces Kidney Radiation Dose During Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study found that patients taking metformin (a diabetes drug) during lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy had significantly lower radiation exposure to their kidneys compared to those not taking metformin. Importantly, tumor radiation doses remained unchanged, suggesting metformin may protect kidneys without reducing treatment effectiveness.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Delivery of Sorafenib Using Nanoparticles in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a PSMA-targeted nanoparticle delivery system for sorafenib, a cancer drug. This targeted approach improved drug solubility and delivery specifically to prostate cancer cells. In laboratory studies, it showed enhanced suppression of cancer cell growth and blood vessel formation compared to standard sorafenib.

items.title: Androgen Receptor Drugs Increase PSMA Uptake for Targeted Therapy
items.summary: This study found that direct androgen receptor blockers (enzalutamide and apalutamide) significantly increase PSMA expression and radioligand uptake in prostate cancer cells. This suggests that combining AR inhibitors with PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy may improve treatment effectiveness by making tumors more visible and responsive to PSMA-directed treatments.

items.title: Real-World Outcomes of Taxane Chemotherapy Discontinuation in mCRPC
items.summary: This study analyzed real-world data showing that many men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer stop taxane chemotherapy early due to side effects. Early discontinuation (fewer cycles) was associated with worse survival outcomes and higher healthcare costs compared to completing more treatment cycles or switching to hormone therapy.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Platinum Nanoparticles for Imaging-Guided Chemoradiotherapy
items.source: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
items.summary: Scientists created PSMA-targeted nanoparticles containing platinum chemotherapy and gadolinium for MRI imaging. These nanoparticles can precisely identify prostate tumors on MRI scans and simultaneously deliver chemotherapy that enhances radiation treatment effectiveness, potentially improving outcomes in locally advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: 18F-rhPSMA-7.3 Detects Recurrent Prostate Cancer Better Than 18F-DCFPyL
items.summary: This case report shows that a newer PSMA PET scan tracer (18F-rhPSMA-7.3) detected recurrent prostate cancer in the bladder area that was missed by the standard 18F-DCFPyL scan. The advantage comes from lower bladder activity, making it easier to see tumors near the bladder.

items.title: Novel Theranostic Targets Beyond PSMA for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review discusses alternative molecular targets for imaging and treating prostate cancer beyond PSMA. Targets include GRPR, FAP, PSCA, CD46, and others. These alternatives may help patients whose tumors have low PSMA expression or expand treatment options for advanced disease.

items.title: Prostatic Acid Phosphatase as Alternative Theranostic Target
items.summary: This article describes prostatic acid phosphatase (ACP3) as a promising alternative to PSMA for imaging and treating prostate cancer. ACP3 is expressed in over 95% of prostate cancers with less off-target uptake in salivary glands and kidneys compared to PSMA. New high-affinity compounds targeting ACP3 show promise for diagnosis and therapy.

items.title: SPECT Scan Metrics Predict Treatment Response During Lu-177 PSMA Therapy
items.summary: This study found that quantitative measurements from post-treatment SPECT scans (taken after lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) correlate with treatment response at the individual tumor level. These measurements may help doctors predict which lesions will respond to therapy and guide treatment decisions in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Mortality Comparison of AR Inhibitors vs Chemotherapy by Heart Disease Status
items.summary: This large population study compared survival in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer receiving hormone pills (AR inhibitors) versus chemotherapy, analyzing those with and without pre-existing heart disease. Results showed similar cancer-related mortality between treatments, providing real-world evidence for treatment decisions in patients with heart conditions.

items.title: PSA Response More Predictive Than Tumor Volume in mHSPC
items.summary: This study compared how well tumor volume (high vs low) and PSA response at 6 months predict outcomes in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with doublet therapy. PSA response appeared to be a stronger predictor of progression and survival than tumor volume, with patients achieving very low PSA having better outcomes regardless of initial tumor burden.

items.title: Deep PSA Response Predicts Better Outcomes in Non-Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This study of 349 Japanese patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer found that achieving very deep PSA declines (>96%) within 6 months of hormone therapy predicts significantly better progression-free survival compared to lesser declines. This suggests that depth of PSA response, not just achieving the standard 90% decline, provides important prognostic information.
